AWPTCM-T33235.objective:
• A port configured to a fixed speed establishes a link at exactly the configured speed with a compliant partner.
  • A link establishes at each supported fixed speed with a matching partner.
  • When an unsupported speed is configured, or the partner is set to an incompatible speed, the link does not come up (or is correctly reported as down), and the port does not enter an unstable or inconsistent state.
  • The port accurately reports the configured fixed speed (not Auto) together with the current link status.
  • A fixed-speed configuration is retained across a pluggable hot-insert/hot-remove, with the link re-establishing at the configured fixed speed.
  • After the configured fixed speed is changed, the port re-resolves to the new speed cleanly, without retaining a stale rate.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Set the port to a supported fixed speed. Confirm the link comes up at exactly that speed, the port reports the fixed speed (not Auto), and traffic is forwarded.
Repeat across the other supported fixed speeds with a matching partner. Confirm link establishment at the exact configured speed and correct reporting in each case.

Configure an unsupported speed on the port, or force a speed mismatch with the partner. Confirm the link does not come up (or is correctly reported as down), and the port remains in a stable, consistent state.
Hot-insert and hot-remove a supported pluggable while the port is set to a fixed speed. Confirm the link re-establishes at the configured fixed speed and the fixed configuration is retained.

Change the configured fixed speed on an established link and confirm the port re-resolves to the new speed cleanly, with reported speed and link status reflecting the new value and no stale rate retained.
